title: The Arrow Dance: a Cobbler's Son, the Altiplano, and the Bronze Furniture of a Country
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Buenos Aires, birth into an immigrant house
stops.date_confidence: attested; the birth neighbourhood, street and parish are named by no source reached, so the coordinate is the canonical city pin and not an address
stops.campa: On the twenty-third of June a son is born in Buenos Aires to Italian immigrant workers, and the family names him Luis Perlotti. The father mends shoes. The house holds no studio and no drawing table. What it holds is the ordinary equipment of the Italian working districts of a city swelling with arrivals, where a trade is something learned from the man who has it and handed on to whoever will sit still long enough. He will fill the plazas of a country with bronze. The street of the house he starts from, and the parish that registers him, are named by no source reached.
suggested_refs: Parish and civil birth registers of Buenos Aires for June 1890, unexamined

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the cobbler dies and the boy goes to work
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year; no month or day given, defaulted to January
stops.campa: The cobbler dies when the boy is nine, and the arithmetic of the household changes inside a week. Luis goes out to be paid. First to the Rigolleau glassworks, where bottles come off the furnace in a heat that does not care how old the hands are. Neither this nor what follows is an art school; both teach material under pressure, which is what a sculptor negotiates with for a life. Then to a cabinetmaker's shop, where wood is cut and joined and finished, and a boy learns what a chisel does to grain and what it does when the grain runs the other way.
suggested_refs: Rigolleau glassworks employment records, Buenos Aires, unexamined

stops.name: Unione e Benevolenza, the mutual society teaches a trade
stops.date_confidence: inferred; the sources record the training but give no year, and the coordinate is approximate for the society in central Buenos Aires
stops.campa: The Italian mutual aid society Unione e Benevolenza keeps classrooms as well as a burial fund, and Perlotti enters them to learn the craft from teachers who came off the same ships his parents did. Here modelling is taught as a trade rather than a vocation: clay, armature, plaster, the mould and the cast, the labour of the workshop before any question of a signature arises. The society exists to make artisans for a city that needs them, and it makes this one a sculptor. He keeps the artisan's habits to the end, running his own moulds and his own patinas in his own shed.
suggested_refs: Archive of the Asociación Unione e Benevolenza, Buenos Aires, for its art and craft classes

stops.name: Academia Nacional de Bellas Artes, the classroom of Correa Morales
stops.date_confidence: inferred; the admission is attested but no year is given, and the coordinate is approximate for the historic academy
stops.campa: Admitted to the Academia Nacional de Bellas Artes, he studies painting under Pío Collivadino and Pablo Ripamonti and sculpture under Lucio Correa Morales, the man who had already begun putting Argentine subjects on Argentine pedestals. Inside fifteen years he will turn this training on faces the Academy keeps no casts of. For now it teaches him the European canon whole: the antique cast, the nude, the balanced contrapposto, proportions agreed on in Rome and Paris and shipped south in plaster. He takes all of it. He draws from the plaster.
suggested_refs: Enrolment records of the Academia Nacional de Bellas Artes, Buenos Aires

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the first Salón Nacional
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year; no month, day, or work title recorded
stops.campa: He shows at the Salón Nacional for the first time at twenty-four. The Salón is the door and everyone in the trade knows it: juries, catalogues, notices in the papers, and behind the papers the municipal committees that decide who gets handed a monument. He will pass through it for the next four decades and the medals will accumulate. Of this first appearance the record preserves a line without a title: which work he sent, and what the jury said of it, are not given by any source reached. He is a name in a catalogue nobody has transcribed.
suggested_refs: Catalogue of the Salón Nacional de Bellas Artes, Buenos Aires, 1914

stops.name: Café Tortoni, the table on Avenida de Mayo
stops.date_confidence: inferred; the gatherings are attested but no source reached dates them
stops.campa: Down the stairs at the Tortoni on Avenida de Mayo the painters and the poets keep a table, and Perlotti keeps a chair at it. Benito Quinquela Martín is there, painting the port of La Boca as though the smoke were the subject. Alfonsina Storni is there, a schoolteacher out of Switzerland by way of Rosario, publishing verse in the weeklies. Twenty-six years on, Perlotti will cut Storni's face into stone above the sea at Mar del Plata, and Quinquela will bolt enamelled murals to the wall of his patio in Caballito. Nothing at the table announces any of that. No source reached dates the gatherings.
suggested_refs: The basement rooms of the Café Tortoni, Avenida de Mayo 825, and their tertulia

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the archaeologists and the americanista
stops.date_confidence: inferred; the influence is attested, the moment is not dated by any source, and the first research pass mislabelled all three men as regionalist writers
stops.campa: Three men turn his eye inland. Eduardo Holmberg the naturalist and Juan Bautista Ambrosetti the ethnographer, founder of the Museo Etnográfico, bring back out of the northwest the pottery, the metalwork and the grave goods of peoples the Academy held no casts of. Ricardo Rojas argues in print for an americanista art grown out of that ground instead of imported from Florence. Perlotti reads them, and then goes to look at what they dug up. From this point the figures he models stop being Greek.
suggested_refs: The Museo Etnográfico Juan B. Ambrosetti, Buenos Aires
Ricardo Rojas, Eurindia (1924)
sources: English Wikipedia, 'Luis Perlotti', which distinguishes the archaeology of Holmberg and Ambrosetti from the regionalist fiction of Rojas

stops.name: The Andean Altiplano, the journeys begin
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year of departure; no towns, itinerary, hosts or duration are named by any source reached, and the coordinate marks the Titicaca basin generically rather than a place he is known to have stood
stops.campa: He begins travelling: through the Americas, and above all through the high country of the Altiplano, the basin around Titicaca where the air is thin, the people are Aymara and Quechua, and the faces are nothing the Academy prepared him to draw. He works from what he sees, and the heads he models afterwards are given the gravity the Academy reserved for gods: flat cheekbones, heavy lids, hair braided and weighty at the shoulder. The sources that record these journeys name no towns, no dates of arrival, no hosts. Only that they run for years, and that he comes back with a subject.
suggested_refs: Any surviving sketchbook or travel diary from Perlotti's American journeys after 1925; none located

stops.name: Buenos Aires, First Prize for La danza de la flecha
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year; the exhibition venue within Buenos Aires is not specified by any source reached
stops.campa: La danza de la flecha takes First Prize at the Municipal Exhibition: a figure some two metres high, an Indian dancer with the arrow, made by a cobbler's son out of the Italian districts who has been up on the Altiplano looking at people. The jury of a European-facing city hands its top award to a subject that city had spent fifty years describing as concluded. He is thirty-seven. The prize is municipal and the plaster is his own. Whether the jury understood what it was crowning, the record does not say.
suggested_refs: Records of the Exposición Municipal de Bellas Artes, Buenos Aires, 1927

segments.name: Seville, and the Figure Set Down

stops.name: Seville, the gold medal at the Ibero-American Exposition
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1929 and dated here to the exposition's opening day; es.wikipedia's 'al año siguiente' phrasing yields 1928 and names no exposition, en.wikipedia names the Ibero-American Exposition of 1929, and es.wikipedia's own article on that exposition fixes its run as 9 May 1929 to 21 June 1930, so no Seville exposition existed in 1928
stops.campa: The Ibero-American Exposition opens at Seville on the ninth of May, Spain's pavilion-city of Latin America laid out around the Plaza de España, and La danza de la flecha is sent across the Atlantic to it. The figure comes back with a gold medal. The arrow dancer, carried from the puna to Buenos Aires and from Buenos Aires to Andalusia, is decorated in the old capital of the empire that spent three centuries governing the people it depicts. He is thirty-eight, and this is the first thing of his to be judged outside Argentina.
suggested_refs: Award lists of the Exposición Iberoamericana de Sevilla, 1929, in the Argentine pavilion section

stops.name: Paraná, the arrow dance set on the roundabout
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year; the siting is specified by the source as the roundabout at Intendente Bertozzi and Avenida Rivadavia
stops.campa: The prize figure is set up permanently in Paraná, on the roundabout where Intendente Bertozzi crosses Avenida Rivadavia, four years after Seville. It stands in traffic, in a river city of Entre Ríos, on a circle that cars go around and around. This is what Perlotti wants and keeps wanting for the rest of his working life: not the salon and not the collector's hall, but the street corner, the school wall, the place where a figure gets looked at by people who did not set out that morning to look at art. The dancer holds the arrow up over the traffic.
suggested_refs: Municipal records of Paraná on the 1933 installation at the Bertozzi and Rivadavia roundabout

stops.name: San Martín, La Serenidad at the Colegio Militar
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year; the exact original siting on the campus is not specified and the coordinate is approximate for the city of San Martín
stops.campa: At the Colegio Militar in San Martín he raises La Serenidad, and the commission opens a vein he will work for the next thirty years: the army as patron. Military schools, regimental plazas, frontier garrisons, flag oaths, busts of the Liberator for towns of two thousand people. The indigenista who models Aymara faces and the monumentalist who supplies the barracks are the same man in the same shed, casting from the same crucible, and no source reached records anyone asking him to explain how the two fit together.
suggested_refs: Commission records of the Colegio Militar de la Nación for the 1931 Monumento a la Serenidad

stops.name: El Palomar, the monument follows the cadets
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day; coordinate corrected to the Colegio Militar de la Nación campus, which is neither the point used in the first research pass nor the centre of El Palomar locality
stops.campa: The Colegio Militar moves to El Palomar and the monument moves with it, transferred on the eighth of December 1938. An image of the Virgen del Carmen is enthroned in the ensemble at the new site, so that the group Perlotti composed acquires a devotion he did not carve. Sixty-six years later, in 2004, under the direction of Colonel Raúl Horacio Gallardo, two cadet figures are added to either side by hands he never met. They stand flanking the Virgen, on a parade ground he had not seen when he made the group, in an arrangement nobody asked him about.
suggested_refs: The Monumento a la Serenidad ensemble at the Colegio Militar de la Nación, El Palomar, as extended in 2004
sources: Spanish Wikipedia, 'Colegio Militar de la Nación' for the campus coordinate

stops.name: Colegio Militar de la Nación, the drummer boy cast three times
stops.date_confidence: inferred; the plaster original is dated 1929 by the source, but no source reached gives a year for the three bronzes commissioned from the Arsenal de Guerra
stops.campa: El Tambor de Tacuarí exists first in plaster, modelled in 1929: Pedro Ríos, the drummer boy of the Tacuarí action of 1811, a child in uniform holding the instrument he is named for. The Arsenal de Guerra is commissioned to cast three bronzes from it. One is set here at the Colegio Militar, one at the entrance portal of the Círculo Militar in Buenos Aires, and one is sent to a town called Concepción. A boy killed in a skirmish more than a century earlier becomes standing furniture in the courtyards where officers are made.
suggested_refs: Arsenal de Guerra casting records for the three bronzes of El Tambor de Tacuarí

stops.name: Concepción, the drummer boy's own country
stops.date_confidence: the work is attested, the town is contested: es.wikipedia 'Luis Perlotti' sends this bronze to Concepción del Uruguay in Entre Ríos, while es.wikipedia 'Tambor de Tacuarí' places the replica in the Plaza 25 de Mayo of Concepción, Corrientes, the old Yaguareté-Corá where Pedro Ríos was born in September 1798; the Corrientes town is pinned here and no source reached reconciles the two
stops.campa: The third bronze goes to a town called Concepción, and the record splits on which one. The article on the sculptor sends it to Concepción del Uruguay in Entre Ríos. The article on the drummer boy himself puts the replica in the Plaza 25 de Mayo of Concepción in Corrientes, the old Yaguareté-Corá, where Pedro Ríos was born in September 1798. Both towns are called Concepción. They stand roughly five hundred kilometres apart, on different rivers, in different provinces, and no source reached reconciles them.
suggested_refs: Plaza 25 de Mayo, Concepción, Corrientes; and the plazas of Concepción del Uruguay, Entre Ríos, for whichever holds the bronze

stops.name: Fortín Olavarría, San Martín on the plaza
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year; coordinate corrected to Wikipedia's point for the locality in the Partido de Rivadavia, the first research pass having placed it 65 to 70 km outside the partido
stops.campa: A bust of José de San Martín for the principal plaza of Fortín Olavarría, a locality of the Partido de Rivadavia out where the province of Buenos Aires runs into flat country and the place names still remember the frontier forts. The commission is small and the town is small. Perlotti takes it as he takes the school walls and the village squares, at every scale offered him, and the head of the Liberator goes up in a settlement most of the country will never have reason to drive through. He is fifty-three.
suggested_refs: The plaza principal of Fortín Olavarría, Partido de Rivadavia, Buenos Aires province
sources: Spanish Wikipedia, 'Fortín Olavarría' and 'Partido de Rivadavia' for the coordinate

stops.name: Plaza Irlanda, the mast of Argentine-Irish brotherhood
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day; coordinate corrected, the first research pass having sat about 1.7 km south-southeast of the plaza
stops.campa: On the sixteenth of November a monument-mast to Argentine-Irish brotherhood is inaugurated in Plaza Irlanda: a bronze relief on a flagpole, in a square named for an island nearly nobody in the neighbourhood has seen. The Irish came to this country as the Italians came, by ship, into a city that already had its own. Perlotti, whose surname arrived the same way, is the sculptor the committee chooses to say so in metal. Whether it chose him for that reason, or because he was the sculptor to hand, is not recorded anywhere reached.
suggested_refs: The Monumento-mástil a la Confraternidad argentino-irlandesa, Plaza Irlanda, Buenos Aires
sources: Spanish Wikipedia, 'Plaza Irlanda' for the coordinate

stops.name: Plaza Dalmacio Vélez Sarsfield, the flag at Floresta
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day
stops.campa: On the twenty-fifth of May, the national date, a Homenaje a la Bandera by Perlotti is inaugurated in the Plaza Dalmacio Vélez Sarsfield in Floresta. Flag, plaza, patriotic date, neighbourhood commission: the whole civic apparatus of the period assembled around one work in bronze. He is now the sculptor Buenos Aires calls when a barrio decides it wants something that will still be standing in fifty years. Six months later the Serenidad will be lifted off its base at San Martín and carried out to the new campus at El Palomar.
suggested_refs: The Homenaje a la Bandera, Plaza Dalmacio Vélez Sarsfield, Floresta, Buenos Aires

stops.name: Parque Los Andes, three peoples in bronze
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year
stops.campa: In Parque Los Andes at Chacarita he installs the Monumento a Los Andes, a bronze group of the Calchaquí, the Tehuelche and the Ona: peoples of the northwestern valleys, of the Patagonian steppe, and of Tierra del Fuego, standing together in a municipal park in a country that had spent the previous sixty years taking them off the map. He models them at full height and in the round, the way the Academy taught him to model senators. The park keeps them. Nobody in 1941 is asked whether the bronze is a monument or an epitaph.
suggested_refs: The Monumento a Los Andes, Parque Los Andes, Chacarita, Buenos Aires

stops.name: Estación Plaza Miserere, the mother underground
stops.date_confidence: undated by any source reached, placed here mid-career by inference; coordinate corrected, the first research pass having sat about 620 m east near Congreso
stops.campa: A Monumento a la Madre by Perlotti is installed in the Plaza Miserere station of Line A, the oldest underground line on the continent, where the trains come in under Once and the platform smells of brake dust and wet coats. Civic sculpture generally wants sky over it and a flight of steps in front of it. This one gets tile and fluorescent light, and a crowd that is not stopping because it has a train to catch. The year of the installation is given by no source reached.
suggested_refs: The Monumento a la Madre on the platform of Estación Plaza Miserere, Línea A, Buenos Aires Underground
sources: Spanish Wikipedia, 'Plaza Miserere' for the coordinate

stops.name: Caminito, the tango composer's head
stops.date_confidence: undated by any source reached; coordinate corrected to the Caminito block in La Boca, the first research pass having sat about 530 m north of it
stops.campa: A bust of the tango composer Juan de Dios Filiberto stands on the Caminito itself, in the painted alley of La Boca that Benito Quinquela Martín spent his life making famous. A second cast of the same head sits inside the Café Tortoni, in the room where Perlotti had been keeping a chair since he was in his twenties. The composer thus holds two addresses in the city: the port alley his music belongs to, and the basement where the men who made his likeness used to drink. Both heads came out of the same mould.
suggested_refs: The bust of Juan de Dios Filiberto at Caminito, La Boca, and its second cast inside the Café Tortoni

stops.name: Plaza Primera Junta, a monument to the barrio itself
stops.date_confidence: undated by any source reached
stops.campa: In Plaza Primera Junta, a short walk from his own front door, Perlotti puts up a monument to the barrio of Caballito, carrying a replica of the historic weathervane the neighbourhood's name is bound up with: a small iron horse that turned on a roof and gave a whole district its word. He lives inside the district he is being asked to commemorate. Everything else he makes is for a nation, an army, a province, a poet. This one is for four hundred blocks of low houses and a subway terminus.
suggested_refs: The Monumento al barrio de Caballito and its weathervane replica, Plaza Primera Junta, Buenos Aires

stops.name: La Perla, Mar del Plata, Alfonsina in stone
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year; coordinate corrected to Balneario La Perla, the first research pass having carried two different and both incorrect points for this one monument
stops.campa: The figure is cut in stone and set on the Paseo Dávila above the beach at La Perla, looking out at the water Alfonsina Storni walked into on the twenty-fifth of October 1938. Verses from her 1925 poem Dolor are inscribed on it. Four years separate the death from the monument; something closer to thirty separates the monument from the basement table on Avenida de Mayo where the sculptor and the poet were both young and neither was anything yet. She is buried at Chacarita, in the city. What stands here is not a grave.
suggested_refs: The Monumento a Alfonsina Storni, Paseo Dávila, Balneario La Perla, Mar del Plata, with its inscription from Dolor (1925)
sources: Spanish Wikipedia, 'Alfonsina Storni' for the Chacarita burial

stops.name: Paseo Dávila, the naturalist on the same promenade
stops.date_confidence: undated by any source reached; coordinate placed on the La Perla frontage per the source's statement that the work stands 'también en el paseo Dávila'
stops.campa: Further along the same promenade stands his monument to Florentino Ameghino, the self-taught naturalist who read the pampa as a fossil bed. Ameghino sits on the same shelf as Holmberg and Ambrosetti, the men who first turned Perlotti's attention to the ground under his own country, and he models him more than once: here on the sea front, and again in plaster at Luján. A few hundred metres of the paseo Dávila separate the naturalist from the poet, and the same hands put both of them there. Both of them face the same water.
suggested_refs: The Monumento a Florentino Ameghino, paseo Dávila, Mar del Plata

stops.name: Luján, the busts at the Biblioteca Ameghino
stops.date_confidence: undated by any source reached; the first research pass wrongly merged this institution with the Complejo Museográfico Enrique Udaondo
stops.campa: At the Asociación Cultural y Biblioteca Ameghino in Luján he leaves plaster busts of Florentino Ameghino and Domingo Faustino Sarmiento, and a bronze reproduction of his own sculpture Viejo. Sarmiento, who wanted the country schooled and its interior remade to a plan, is a head Perlotti cuts more than once for this town alone. The library is not a museum and charges nothing at the door. The works sit in the room where the readers sit, at the height of a reader's eye.
suggested_refs: The Asociación Cultural y Biblioteca Ameghino, Luján, holding the plaster busts and the bronze Viejo

stops.name: Luján, the cabildo plaque and the school busts
stops.date_confidence: undated by any source reached; coordinate approximate for the town centre
stops.campa: Three further works are scattered across the same small town. A bronze plaque in the Cabildo de Luján carries a copy of the 1917 decree that founded the Complejo Museográfico Enrique Udaondo. A bust of Sarmiento stands at School No. 12. A bust of the intendente Juan Bautista Barnech stands at the Escuela Normal Mixta Florentino Ameghino. A founding decree, a schoolmaster, a mayor: Perlotti works the whole civic inventory of a provincial town, in the order it is offered to him. No source reached gives a year for any of the three.
suggested_refs: The bronze plaque of the 1917 founding decree, Cabildo de Luján; the busts at Escuela No. 12 and the Escuela Normal Mixta Florentino Ameghino

stops.name: Cementerio de Luján, the mourning women
stops.date_confidence: undated by any source reached; coordinate approximate for the municipal cemetery
stops.campa: In the municipal cemetery of Luján stand two works in a register he otherwise rarely enters: Las Dolorosas, and a Cristo en la Cruz. Which families ordered them, and in what year, no source reached says. The indigenista who models Aymara heads and the monumentalist who supplies flag oaths to the army turns here to the mourning women and the crucified body, the oldest commission in European sculpture and the one his Academy training was actually designed for.
suggested_refs: Las Dolorosas and Cristo en la Cruz in the municipal cemetery of Luján, Buenos Aires province

stops.name: Suipacha, the Liberator in Plaza Balcarce
stops.date_confidence: undated by any source reached
stops.campa: A monument to José de San Martín in the Plaza Balcarce at Suipacha, a town of the western pampa on the line out toward Mercedes. The Liberator is the most reproduced face in the republic, and the demand on Perlotti does not slacken; nor does the model change much from one commission to the next. What changes is the plaza, and the size of the crowd on the day of the unveiling. He supplies his share of the face: Suipacha, Fortín Olavarría, the Valle de Uco, and wherever else a committee writes to him.
suggested_refs: The Monumento a San Martín, Plaza Balcarce, Suipacha, Buenos Aires province

stops.name: Chascomús, Los Libres del Sur
stops.date_confidence: undated by any source reached; coordinate approximate for the town centre, the monument site not confirmed
stops.campa: Los Libres del Sur stands at Chascomús, for the rising of 1839 in which the landowners and militia of the southern countryside took arms against Juan Manuel de Rosas and were broken beside the lagoon. Perlotti is commissioned a century afterward by the town that lost the battle. Provincial monuments in this country are very often monuments to defeats, and the sculptor who supplies them is asked for dignity rather than triumph: standing figures, level gaze, no raised sword.
suggested_refs: The Monumento a Los Libres del Sur, Chascomús, Buenos Aires province

stops.name: Río Gallegos, the flag oath in bronze
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year; coordinate approximate for the city centre
stops.campa: For School No. 19 in Río Gallegos he casts a bronze bas-relief, Juramento de la Bandera: children with their hands held out over the flag, fixed to a wall in a wind-scoured town on the estuary at the bottom of the continent, some two thousand six hundred kilometres from his shed in Caballito. The children of Santa Cruz swear to a flag modelled by a man the record never places in their province. The relief makes the journey south by ship or by rail. Whether the sculptor ever does, no source reached records.
suggested_refs: The Juramento de la Bandera bas-relief, Escuela No. 19, Río Gallegos, Santa Cruz

stops.name: Corrientes, the Monumento a Mitre
stops.date_confidence: the work and its attribution are attested by both es.wikipedia and en.wikipedia, but no source reached gives an inauguration date or names the plaza; the year here is an inference only
stops.campa: A Monumento a Mitre by Perlotti stands in the city of Corrientes, up where the Paraná turns toward Paraguay and the summers are unbearable. Bartolomé Mitre, who commanded and wrote and governed and translated Dante, is the kind of national figure a provincial capital wants in bronze on a plaza. Both encyclopedic accounts of Perlotti's work name the monument. Neither gives a date, an inauguration, or a location within the city. When was it put up, and on which plaza does it stand?
suggested_refs: Municipal records of the city of Corrientes for the Monumento a Bartolomé Mitre and its inauguration

stops.name: La Rioja, the monument to the Diaguita
stops.date_confidence: undated by any source reached; the plaza within the city is not specified and the coordinate is the city centre
stops.campa: In the city of La Rioja he raises a monument to the Diaguita, the people of the northwestern valleys whose pottery and worked bronze had travelled south to the Museo Etnográfico in wooden cases and reached him first as objects under glass, years before he went to look at the country they came from. Neither the plaza nor the year of the inauguration is given by any source reached. What is certain is that here the figures stand on that country's own ground, in the province the objects were carried out of.
suggested_refs: The Monumento a los Diaguitas, city of La Rioja, Argentina

stops.name: El Manzano Histórico, El retorno a la patria
stops.date_confidence: undated by any source reached; the source places the work in the Valle de Uco, localidad de Tunuyán, and the coordinate is the Monumento del Retorno at El Manzano Histórico, whose own article names the monument but does not name its sculptor
stops.campa: El retorno a la patria stands in the Valle de Uco, at El Manzano Histórico under the cordillera, where tradition places José de San Martín's rest on the way back down from Chile. The monument marks a homecoming rather than a departure: the army coming back through the pass, the campaign finished, the mountains behind rather than ahead. Perlotti had already cast the Andes in bronze once, in a park at Chacarita. This is the only work of his that stands at their foot.
suggested_refs: The Monumento del Retorno at El Manzano Histórico, Tunuyán, Mendoza
sources: Spanish Wikipedia, 'El Manzano Histórico' for the coordinate

stops.name: Río Gallegos, the bust of Piedrabuena
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year; no source reached shows Perlotti travelling to Santa Cruz to see either of his southern works in place
stops.campa: Fourteen years after the flag relief a second work goes south: a bust of Luis Piedrabuena, the navigator who kept an Argentine flag flying on the Patagonian coast and a house on the Isla Pavón in the Santa Cruz river at a time when there was almost nobody else on that coast to see either. Perlotti is sixty-eight and still taking commissions from the far end of the country. He has now furnished the far south twice over with faces cast in a workshop in Caballito. Nothing in the record puts him below the Río Negro.
suggested_refs: The bust of Luis Piedrabuena at Río Gallegos, Santa Cruz

stops.name: Buenos Aires, explaining the Welsh monument to Clarín
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day of publication; the Clarín page itself was not reached and the statement survives here at one remove, as quoted by es.wikipedia
stops.campa: Five years before the monument is unveiled in Chubut, Clarín prints the sculptor describing it in his own words, which he almost never does anywhere the record can follow. An ascending parallelepiped for the base. A woman three metres high on top of it for the spirit of the Welsh undertaking. Two reliefs below: the landing, with the pastor and the Bible and the barque Mimosa lying offshore, and the Tehuelche holding out his hand. He is explaining a Patagonian monument to readers in Buenos Aires who will mostly never stand in front of it. He is seventy. The thing itself will not be unveiled for another five years.
stops.quote: He concebido el monumento a los Galeses con una gran base que tiene la forma de un paralelepípedo ascendente.
stops.quote_source: Luis Perlotti in Clarín, 9 November 1960, as quoted in Spanish Wikipedia, 'Luis Perlotti'; the original page was not reached
suggested_refs: Clarín, 9 November 1960, Perlotti's statement on the Monumento a los Galeses; original not reached
sources: Spanish Wikipedia, 'Luis Perlotti', quoting Clarín, 9 November 1960

stops.name: Puerto Madryn, the Welsh on the rambla
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day
stops.campa: On the twenty-eighth of July, the centenary of the landing, the Monumento a los Galeses is inaugurated on the seafront rambla of Puerto Madryn. Welsh families had come ashore here off the Mimosa in 1865, onto a coast with no fresh water and no wood, and dug into the bank at Punta Cuevas to get through the first winter. Perlotti had described the design to a newspaper five years before it was cut. His woman now stands three metres high above the two reliefs of that arrival, facing the gulf the Mimosa crossed.
stops.quote: Sobre la parte superior he puesto una figura de mujer, de tres metros de altura, que simboliza el espíritu de la gesta galesa...
stops.quote_source: Luis Perlotti in Clarín, 9 November 1960, on the Monumento a los Galeses, as quoted in Spanish Wikipedia, 'Luis Perlotti'
suggested_refs: The Monumento a los Galeses on the rambla of Puerto Madryn, inaugurated 28 July 1965

stops.name: Punta Cuevas, the Tehuelche at the point
stops.date_confidence: undated by any source reached; the coordinate is reconstructed from the headland's position at the southern end of the Puerto Madryn shore, since no coordinate-bearing article for Punta Cuevas exists, and should be checked against the municipality
stops.campa: South of the town, at Punta Cuevas where the first Welsh cut their shelters into the bank, Perlotti sets a Monumento al Indio Tehuelche. On the Welsh monument the Tehuelche is one panel of two, a relief on a base, an episode inside somebody else's arrival story. Here he stands by himself, on the point, at full height, for the people who met the newcomers on a coast the newcomers could not yet read. Perlotti had been modelling this figure, under one name and another, for forty years.
stops.quote: El otro relieve representa al Tehuelche, hijo de la tierra, tendiendo su mano de paz a los recién llegados.
stops.quote_source: Luis Perlotti in Clarín, 9 November 1960, describing the Tehuelche relief on the Monumento a los Galeses, as quoted in Spanish Wikipedia, 'Luis Perlotti'
suggested_refs: The Monumento al Indio Tehuelche at Punta Cuevas, south of Puerto Madryn, near the Museo del Desembarco

stops.name: Pujol 644, Caballito, the house bought
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year; coordinate corrected to the museum article's own point, the first research pass having sat about a kilometre southeast near Plaza Primera Junta
stops.campa: He buys the property at Pujol 642 and 644 in Caballito and starts rebuilding it around what he means it to become. At the entrance to the patio Benito Quinquela Martín hangs two large murals in enamelled iron, the colours of the Riachuelo carried inland to a sculptor's courtyard eight kilometres from the water. The friendship that began at a basement table on Avenida de Mayo is now bolted to a wall. Two halls go in for exhibiting finished work, and a library goes in beside them. He is fifty-eight.
suggested_refs: The house-studio at Pujol 642/644, Caballito, with the two enamelled-iron murals by Benito Quinquela Martín at the patio entrance
sources: Spanish Wikipedia, 'Museo de Esculturas Luis Perlotti'

stops.name: Pujol 644, the neighbourhood let in
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year
stops.campa: He begins taking people through the house himself. Not collectors and not critics: the neighbourhood, walked from room to room by the man who made what is standing in them. These are the years of his heaviest commission load, and he spends the afternoons this way. A working sculptor's house in Caballito is opened, on his own initiative and at his own hours, to whoever on the block wants to come in and look at what a plaster figure looks like before it is bronze.
suggested_refs: The guided visits Perlotti conducted personally at Pujol 644 from 1954
sources: Spanish Wikipedia, 'Museo de Esculturas Luis Perlotti'

stops.name: Parque Rivadavia, the last monument at home
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day
stops.campa: On the fifteenth of October the Monumento a la Madre is inaugurated in Parque Rivadavia, a few blocks from his front door, in the park where Caballito buys its second-hand books on a Sunday. He is seventy-five. It is the last of his monuments to be inaugurated in the neighbourhood he lives in. Of the two Monumentos a la Madre he made for this city, this is the one with sky over it; the other stands on a platform under Once, in the fluorescent light.
suggested_refs: The Monumento a la Madre, Parque Rivadavia, Caballito, inaugurated 15 October 1965

stops.name: Punta del Este, in front of the casino
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day; the first research pass added 'while vacationing', which no source states and which has been removed
stops.campa: On the twenty-fifth of January, in the street in front of the casino at Punta del Este, Perlotti is struck by a vehicle. He is seventy-eight years old and has been working for sixty of them. What the record gives is the town, the casino frontage, and the date. Why he is in a Uruguayan resort in January is stated by no source reached; the summer season is the obvious answer and is written down nowhere that can be checked. He is not treated where he fell. He is taken to Montevideo.
suggested_refs: Uruguayan press reports of 25 and 26 January 1969 on the accident at Punta del Este; not reached

stops.name: Montevideo, the Hospital Británico
stops.date_confidence: es.wikipedia states in prose that he died at the Hospital Británico in Montevideo of injuries from the Punta del Este accident, while en.wikipedia's infobox gives Punta del Este as the place of death; the split is recorded and not resolved, and the coordinate is derived from the hospital's address at Avenida Italia 2420, its own article carrying none
stops.campa: He dies the same day at the Hospital Británico on Avenida Italia in Montevideo, a hundred and thirty kilometres from the street where he was hit. The Spanish account is specific about it: injured at Punta del Este, in front of the casino, dead at the British Hospital in the capital. The English account puts his death at Punta del Este and stops there. Two encyclopedias, one man, two cities for the same afternoon. Where he is buried afterwards is named by nothing reached at all.

stops.name: Pujol 644, ordinance 27.726
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day
stops.campa: Perlotti left the house and everything standing in it to the city. The city takes four years to say yes. Municipal ordinance 27.726, dated the twenty-third of May 1973, formalises the acceptance of the property at Pujol 644 and its entire artistic holdings, and a further ordinance three years after that refines the terms. A shorter account has circulated saying the house became a public museum in 1969, on his death. The ordinance says otherwise. The doors will go on saying otherwise for another seventeen years.
suggested_refs: Municipal ordinance 27.726 of 23 May 1973 and its 1976 amendment, Buenos Aires
sources: Spanish Wikipedia, 'Museo de Esculturas Luis Perlotti'

stops.name: Pujol 644, the museum opens
stops.date_confidence: attested to the month; no day given, defaulted to the first
stops.campa: In 1987 Professor César A. Fioravanti takes up the project of actually opening the donated house, and in December 1990 the Museo de Esculturas Luis Perlotti receives its first public. Twenty-one years have gone by since the sculptor died, and thirty-six since he first walked the neighbours through these rooms himself. The collection runs past sixteen hundred pieces: wood, marble, bronze, ceramic, reconstituted stone, drawings, prints. The two Quinquela murals are still on the patio wall where he bolted them.

stops.name: Pujol 644, the house inside a newer house
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day; the City of Buenos Aires museum page gives the restoration span as 2003 to 2008
stops.campa: A design competition in 2004 hands the museum's renovation to the architect Mario Roberto Álvarez, and on the twenty-second of December 2008 the rebuilt building reopens. Perlotti's house now stands inside a modern one. The rooms where a cobbler's son kept his moulds and his patinas hold an environmental management certificate, an accessibility certificate and an equality seal. La Danza de la Flecha is in the halls, and Despertar de la Raza, and the annex on Nicasio Oroño holds more.
